finalists.label: Erythema multiforme
finalists.why: The candidate has specific findings such as erythema and helical thickening as well as numerous small blisters on both ears and similar vesicles at the upper and lower vermillion border.

finalists.label: Viral exanthem
finalists.why: The candidate accounts for the intensely pruritic skin eruption, episode of malaise and headache, and various skin lesions, despite negative results for several viruses.

finalists.label: Sun-induced immune-mediated reaction
finalists.why: The candidate is supported by the appearance of symptoms approximately 24 hours after intensive sun exposure.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of specific skin lesions such as erythema, helical thickening, and small blisters on both ears, as well as the lack of evidence against Erythema multiforme, decided the final comparison.

support_spans: Erythema and helical thickening as well as numerous small blisters, 2 to 3 mm in diameter, were present on both ears
Similar vesicles were observed at the upper and lower vermillion border
Several erythematous papules and crusts were located on the cheeks, neck, and lower arms
Serum parvovirus B19 (PVB19) IgM and IgG antibodies were detectable
PVB19 DNA was found (viral load of 0.2 PVB19 DNA copies/β-globin gene copy, or 33,438 copies/μg of isolated DNA) in lesional skin biopsy specimen
appeared approximately 24 hours after intensive sun exposure
contradict_spans: Standard phototesting with UV-A and UV-B was unremarkable
